prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "Apply embedding model expertise to this task". The fixture contains a plausible happy path, an adjacent-skill decoy, one invalid or partial state, and a recovery condition that must be demonstrated rather than assumed. The acceptance boundary is embedding-systems: Define the semantic unit and downstream decision before selecting an embedding model. The adjacent computer-vision discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

requirements: judged multilingual retrieval queries plus labeled duplicate pairs and long/empty/degenerate inputs
old/new vector snapshots, corpus/backfill manifests and representation-aware cache fixtures
representation manifest and embedding/index seam fixtures covering identity, dimension, normalization, metric and namespace mismatches
latency, storage and cost measurements plus cutover/rollback controls
separate provider fact, observed response receipt, empirical result and unavailable-evidence labels
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual embedding-systems boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=implementation; near-neighbor=computer-vision), keep vector-search-systems responsible for ANN/index mechanics, and not absorb either neighboring responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Define the semantic unit and downstream decision before selecting an embedding model.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, representation manifest, embedding/index seam ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.

Evaluate downstream retrieval/classification/clustering behavior on labeled cases, compare model revisions, test long/short/multilingual inputs and zero/degenerate vectors, assert index representation compatibility, and measure latency/storage/cost with provider or index identity recorded.

The result must not take the tempting shortcut prohibited by this skill: Do not compare vectors from incompatible models, infer absolute meaning from similarity thresholds without calibration, or choose dimensions solely from benchmark headlines.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (documented provider/model/version/task facts separated from observed response behavior; preprocessing/dimension/normalization representation identity; input limit, truncation, batching/cache and degenerate-vector behavior; labeled downstream quality plus latency/cost evidence; versioned migration/backfill/coverage/cutover/rollback and drift-canary evidence), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
